title: Start here
intro: holita admin helps you follow trucks, review trips and faults, and manage your fleet and devices. The Storybook tree follows the admin menu in the same order; pages opened from a menu item sit underneath it.
review: Choose English or Bulgarian with Language in the Storybook toolbar. Theme and the phone viewport let you review the same screen in a different appearance or width. Open a state, then use its controls to explore.
sourcesNote: Badges describe the data available in the admin today. Storybook itself uses fixed examples: it does not contact Karma or send commands to trucks. Fleet records and preferences are stored in holita; this review uses a demo fleet.

entries.overview: See the fleet totals and recent activity from demo telemetry.
entries.alerts: Review and acknowledge alerts generated from demo telemetry.
entries.trips: Browse trips and open their details using demo telemetry.
entries.vehicles: Manage the selected fleet’s vehicle records, profiles and odometer settings in holita.
entries.drivers: Manage driver records and assignments in holita; scorecards use demo telemetry.
entries.devices: Manage tracking-device records and vehicle assignments in holita.
entries.maintenance: Plan and record service work for the selected fleet in holita.
entries.karma-cars: Open trucks from the connected Karma account, then review their trips, location, events, eData, diagnostics and device settings.
entries.karma-administration: Read users, roles, projects, time zones and API information from the connected Karma account.
entries.vehicle-groups: Organize the selected fleet’s vehicles into groups stored in holita.
entries.general: Choose the fleet name, units and time zone, stored in holita.
entries.karma-monitoring: See truck connectivity, retained fault reports and the Branch event log. Default retention is 10 days.
entries.karma-settings: Set monitoring intervals, fault reads and log retention for the selected Branch.

statusTitle: Device settings: what is proven as of 2 November 2026
proven: Interval change on CB1147TP: parameter 662 changed from 30 to 60 seconds.
Diagnostic history displayed three real faults.
Five real 411 connection reports were received. This proves receiving reports; requesting the check from the admin still needs a real-truck trial.
unproven: Adding a parameter through the admin.
Reading rules and changing a rule.
Requesting the 411 connection check from the admin.
logger: Fault logger read: the truck answers “not acknowledged”, so no faults are retrieved this way. The three proven faults came from diagnostic history.
report: Send the full story title from the sidebar, explain what looks wrong or what you expected, and attach a screenshot. Include the Language, Theme and viewport you used.
buildingBlocksNote: Design System contains the shared layout, colours, controls and panels used across the admin.
